name: Janu Tokyo
positioning: The first hotel of Janu, an Aman Group brand, in the Azabudai Hills neighbourhood of Minato, with a large wellness centre and rooms designed by Jean-Michel Gathy
best_for: Travelers who want group fitness classes and a large wellness centre in central Tokyo
Travelers who want a base in Azabudai Hills, close to Roppongi and Toranomon

facts.text: Janu Tokyo is set in Azabudai Hills, a new neighbourhood in Minato.
Janu Tokyo is close to Roppongi and Toranomon.
Janu Tokyo is the first hotel of Janu, a brand that is part of the Aman Group.
Condé Nast Traveler describes Azabudai as Tokyo's newest luxury enclave, with boutiques from the world's biggest high-end brands.
The hotel occupies the lower floors of a corporate tower rather than its top.
Janu Tokyo has a 4,000 square metre wellness centre.
Janu Tokyo has eight dining and socialising destinations, including Janu Mercato for all-day Italian dining.
At Sumi, a sumibiyaki omakase counter, 13 guests sit at the kitchen counter as the chef prepares a multi-course meat and fish menu enhanced with charcoal smoke.
The Janu boutique sells Aman Essentials beauty, fragrance and wellness products, along with objects and prints made by local artists and artisans.
Janu Tokyo was named to Condé Nast Traveler's Hot List 2025.

highlights.text: Janu Tokyo has one of the largest wellness spaces and gyms in the city, with workouts from Pilates to high impact circuit training.
The wellness spaces include several dedicated studios for activities such as aerial yoga, sound baths and spin classes.
The rooms and suites were designed by architect Jean-Michel Gathy of Denniston.
Room design reinterprets Japanese touchstones in modern ways: shoji screens become metal-and-fabric rolling panels, and stone and porcelain basins take the place of hinoki soaking tubs.
The hotel has a large, resort-sized pool.

considerations.text: Views from the Deluxe Rooms are not as expansive as those from the suites.
Condé Nast Traveler found the language barrier higher than at some other ultra-luxury hotels in Tokyo, though service was attentive and kind.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning.

sources.title: Condé Nast Traveler: Janu Tokyo review
